implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) was approved 2026-09-22 and replaces the December 2025 template policy. Access procedures are in the engineering handbook.

Workforce accounts are created in the identity provider from People Operations tickets and federated to the cloud consoles, repository, support tools, and admin console. Accounts are disabled in the identity provider on the last day. Gaps: production database access uses one shared break-glass role; quarterly reviews cover the identity provider only; two former contractors kept local repository accounts outside single sign-on (removed 2026-09-04). Customer administrators manage their own users' accounts in their tenant.
evidence: IdP user export; onboarding and termination tickets; repository member list

implementation_statement: Role-based access inside each tenant (administrator, manager, worker) is enforced by the application. Tenant isolation is enforced in the data access layer by scoping every query to the tenant ID. Gap: automated isolation tests cover 80% of API endpoints and are not a merge gate; there is no database-level second layer.
evidence: Isolation test report; penetration test report (2026-01)
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: continuously validate access to data); SOC 2 CC6.1

implementation_statement: Code changes need one reviewer who is not the author. Gap: repository administrators can bypass branch protection; 3 bypasses occurred in the 90 days before fieldwork, none documented.

Engineers have read-only console roles by default. Gaps: CI deploy keys have broad read and write permissions across the production account; the shared break-glass role is used for routine fixes; all 21 engineers have write access to staging, which holds production data copies.
evidence: Cloud IAM export; CI secret inventory
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: limit administrative access); SOC 2 CC6.3

implementation_statement: Cloud management API calls are logged by the provider's audit logging. Gap: SQL commands run through the shared break-glass role are not recorded, and database sessions are not attributable to a person.
evidence: Cloud audit log sample; vault checkout log
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (deception risk: public statement that every access is logged)

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks workforce accounts after 10 failed attempts. The platform rate-limits worker and customer sign-in attempts by account and source address.
Device management locks laptops after 5 minutes idle.
Customer sessions end after 12 hours or 60 minutes idle. Gap: the internal admin console and cloud console sessions last up to 12 hours with no re-authentication for sensitive actions.

There is no network VPN. All administrative access is to SaaS and cloud consoles through single sign-on with MFA; server shell access uses the provider's session manager, with no inbound SSH from the internet.
evidence: Network rules export; session manager settings
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: secure remote access)

implementation_statement: Awareness and training requirements are in POL-05 (P06), approved 2026-09-22.
All staff complete security awareness training at hire and annually; semiannual phishing simulations started in 2026.
evidence: Training completion report (98%); phishing simulation results

implementation_statement: Gap: engineers receive no secure coding training. Planned: annual secure coding course for all 21 engineers, first completion by 2026-12-15.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: train your engineers in secure coding)

implementation_statement: Logging and review requirements are in POL-02 section 4.9 (P06).

Cloud management events, identity provider sign-ins, and application audit events (sign-ins, role changes, exports, view-as-tenant) are logged. Gap: object-level access logging is off for the payroll export bucket, and database query logging is off.
Application audit events record tenant, user, action, object, source address, and time. Cloud audit records follow the provider's format.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: no one reviews cloud audit logs, privileged sessions, or view-as-tenant sessions. Planned: weekly review of privileged activity and a monthly review of view-as-tenant sessions from 2026-11-02, with alerting for unusual cloud API activity.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: monitor activity on your network); SOC 2 CC7.2

implementation_statement: Audit logs are protected by provider access controls. Gap: logs stay in the production account, where the same administrator roles could delete them.
Gap: cloud audit logs use the provider's default 90-day history and application logs are kept 30 days. Planned: 1-year retention in a separate log archive account by 2026-11-30.
Audit record generation for management events is on by default at the provider and cannot be disabled by workload teams.

implementation_statement: Change management and secure development requirements are in POL-01 section 4.8 (P06).
Most production resources are defined in infrastructure as code. Gap: 3 storage buckets and 2 queue policies are configured by hand.

All application and infrastructure changes go through pull requests with one approval and automated tests before deployment. Gap: administrator bypass of branch protection and undocumented emergency changes (SOC 2 CC8.1).
Container and database settings are defined in code. Gap: no cloud configuration benchmark or alert for risky changes such as public storage access.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: ensure proper configuration)

implementation_statement: Minimal container base images; only the load balancer is internet-facing; unused cloud services are blocked by account policy.

Cloud resources are inventoried from infrastructure code and the provider's inventory service; laptops from device management. Gap: 4 corporate SaaS apps are outside single sign-on and missing from the SaaS inventory.
Contingency planning requirements will be added to POL-03 with the DR plan due 2027-01-31.
Gap: no documented DR or contingency plan. The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-09-22 and sets RTO 2 hours and RPO 15 minutes for time capture. Plan due 2027-01-31.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)); customer MSA (99.9% SLA); SOC 2 A1.2; CC9.1

implementation_statement: One database restore test in January 2026 took 5 hours, longer than the 2-hour RTO. No regional failover test. Planned: semiannual restore and failover tests from 2026-12.

The managed database keeps 7 days of point-in-time recovery; daily snapshots are copied to a second region; object storage is versioned. Gap: all copies are in the production account and can be deleted by production administrators.
Production can be rebuilt from infrastructure code and container images. Gap: no written recovery runbook, and only the Platform Engineering Lead has done a rebuild.
Identification and authentication requirements are in POL-02 (P06).
Every workforce user has a unique identity-provider account; all workforce access to in-scope systems goes through single sign-on. Exception: the shared break-glass database role (see AC-2, IA-4).
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: require secure passwords and authentication)

implementation_statement: MFA is required for all privileged accounts; the 6 engineers with production access use hardware security keys.
evidence: Conditional access policy; key registration report

implementation_statement: MFA is required for all workforce sign-ins (MFA everywhere).
Identifiers are unique for all people and services except the shared break-glass role and the 2 shared CI deploy keys.

Workforce passwords follow identity provider policy (length and banned-password list). Worker and customer passwords are salted and hashed with an adaptive algorithm. Gaps: 2 long-lived static CI cloud keys (older than 1 year) and third-party API keys are never rotated; there is no secret scanning on push.
evidence: CI secret inventory; key age report
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: store passwords securely)

implementation_statement: Customer users authenticate with platform accounts or their own SAML single sign-on. MFA is enforced for customer administrators and optional for workers.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-09-22 (P06).
Planned: incident response training for on-call engineers and support leads before the tabletop exercise on 2026-11-18.
Gap: the plan has never been tested. First tabletop (the P08 scenario) scheduled 2026-11-18.

Incidents are handled by the on-call engineer and the IT Manager. The P08 runbook for cloud credential compromise was approved 2026-09-22. Gap: forensic retainer not yet in place (insurer panel only).
Security incidents are logged in the engineering ticket system with a security label. Gap: no severity scheme or monthly review.

Internal reporting is through the on-call page and a security chat channel. Gap: the customer notice step did not reflect the 72-hour and 48-hour contract terms until the P08 matrix; no per-customer security contact list.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)); customer DPA (72-hour notice); Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)

implementation_statement: Incident response plan elements are in POL-03 and the P08 runbook.

The cloud provider sanitizes storage media under its own controls (inherited, per its SOC 2 report). Laptops are wiped through device management before reissue; retired laptops go to a certified recycler with certificates.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: dispose of sensitive data securely)

implementation_statement: Physical access to data centers is controlled by the cloud provider (inherited). The office holds no production systems.

regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: test for common vulnerabilities)

implementation_statement: Provider DDoS protection and a web application firewall front the load balancer.

implementation_statement: TLS 1.2 or higher on all public endpoints and to sub-processor APIs; TLS between services inside the cluster.

implementation_statement: Database, snapshots, object storage, and queues are encrypted at rest in production and staging.

regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: heed credible security warnings)

implementation_statement: EDR on all laptops with alerts to the IT Manager. Production containers are rebuilt from scanned images and do not accept file uploads for execution.

Uptime, error-rate, and performance monitoring with on-call alerts; EDR alerts for laptops. Gap: the provider's threat detection service is not enabled and there are no alerts for unusual API activity, bulk object reads, or snapshot copies.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: monitor activity on your network); SOC 2 CC7.2
